The revised head resolves the previous settlement-integration concern, and no blocking patch defect was found. **Priority:** P1 **Reviewed head:** `dda04893deb433098864bc65a6fdf5208c0f4f3e` ## Review scores | Measure | Result | What it means | |---|---|---| | **Overall readiness** | 🐚 platinum hermit **(4/6)** | A focused owner-level repair with credible native integration evidence, useful regression coverage, and no blocking findings. | | **Proof confidence** | 🐚 platinum hermit **(4/6)** | Sufficient (logs): Captured exact-head evidence reports real Gateway/native Codex recovery after injected HTTP401 failures, same-thread authenticated resume, and rejected cross-conversation takeover; protocol fixtures separately cover refusal delivery without retry or fallback. | | **Patch quality** | 🐚 platinum hermit **(4/6)** | No actionable review findings were identified. | ## Verification | Check | Result | Evidence | |---|---|---| | **Real behavior** | Verified | Sufficient (logs): Captured exact-head evidence reports real Gateway/native Codex recovery after injected HTTP401 failures, same-thread authenticated resume, and rejected cross-conversation takeover; protocol fixtures separately cover refusal delivery without retry or fallback. | | **Evidence reviewed** | 13 items | Current main still contains the defect: Fetched main retains the idle/notLoaded-only adoption checks. Its cleanup still retains ordinary threads only after success, and its refusal classifier lacks misalignmentPolicyViolation.
Settled failure excludes interrupted outcomes: Finalization records failed settlement only after native failure completion and excludes cancellation, timeout, client closure, and execution disconnect.
Existing retention owner is reused: Cleanup retains the existing configuration receipt under the binding lease and physical-client identity check. Incognito failure, one-shot cleanup, supervision, native-model preservation, and ring-zero exclusions remain. | | **Findings** | None | None. | | **Security** | None | None. | ## How this fits together The Codex plugin connects OpenClaw chat turns to native Codex conversations. Its lifecycle owner retains reusable threads, validates later requests, and returns terminal outcomes for chat delivery. ```mermaid flowchart TD A[Chat message] --> B[Codex conversation owner] B --> C[Ownership and configuration checks] C --> D[Native Codex turn] D --> E[Terminal outcome] E --> F[Visible reply or refusal] E --> G[Retain safely settled thread] G --> C ``` ## Before merge None.

Members: - `canonical`: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/138835 - Documents the completed-failure status and refusal-classification defects addressed here. - `same_root_cause`: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/138846 - Original open repair proposal explicitly credited and replaced by this PR. Proposal only: this assessment does not dispatch repair, suppress jobs, mutate sibling items, close, or merge anything. ### Technical review Best possible solution: Retain settled failures through the existing subscription owner while preserving configuration attestation and terminal refusals; distinguishing safe failure from success and interrupted teardown justifies the small state expansion. Do we have a high-confidence way to reproduce the issue? Yes—the native HTTP401 → completed failure → later message sequence is supported by current-main source and supplied before/after results; this review did not execute it. Is this the best way to solve the issue? Yes. Repairing retention at its lifecycle owner avoids unnecessary reconfiguration, while extending the existing refusal diagnostic avoids a competing core error contract. AGENTS.md: found and applied where relevant. Native system-error handling clears running state while retaining the error flag. Otherwise resume can acknowledge the thread while ignoring overrides; systemError alone is insufficient. ([`codex-rs/app-server/src/request_processors/thread_processor.rs:4183`](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/3d2ee51ca2d5db578f328aa75e20aa22c0197c9a/codex-rs/app-server/src/request_processors/thread_processor.rs#L4183), [3d2ee51ca2d5](https://github.com/openai/codex/commit/3d2ee51ca2d5db578f328aa75e20aa22c0197c9a)) - **Native refusal confirmation remains separate:** The native contract makes the policy category terminal and defines a distinct confirmed-override submission. The patch does not introduce that override metadata or treat later ordinary input as confirmation. ([`codex-rs/app-server/README.md:1914`](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/3d2ee51ca2d5db578f328aa75e20aa22c0197c9a/codex-rs/app-server/README.md#L1914), [3d2ee51ca2d5](https://github.com/openai/codex/commit/3d2ee51ca2d5db578f328aa75e20aa22c0197c9a)) Likely related people: - **Peter Steinberger:** Suggested for follow-up; no historical authorship or introduction is verified. Ready to land at `dda04893deb433098864bc65a6fdf5208c0f4f3e`.

- Root cause: completed native failures lost the retained configuration owner, and typed misalignment errors missed the existing refusal diagnostic.
- Fix: retain settled failed ordinary conversations through the existing owner; reuse the established refusal delivery and no-replay path. No new SDK error, configuration option, schema or protocol change.
- Independent native/Gateway proof: baseline HTTP401 → `systemError` → false runner rejection; repaired ordinary and authenticated manual continuation completes on the same thread. Cross-conversation takeover is rejected for active and stopped threads. Terminal requests do not replay; ordinary retry succeeds.
- CI: [run 33982203491](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/33982203491) passed on this exact head. Local exact-head review has no findings or security concerns and accepts the product proof. The latest public review has no blockers or rank-up actions.

Validation commands:

```sh
OPENCLAW_VITEST_MAX_WORKERS=1 node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/codex/src/app-server/run-attempt-thread-cleanup.test.ts extensions/codex/src/app-server/event-projector.terminal-errors.test.ts extensions/codex/src/app-server/run-attempt.settlement.test.ts
OPENCLAW_E2E_USE_PREBUILT_DIST=1 OPENCLAW_VITEST_MAX_WORKERS=1 node scripts/run-vitest.mjs test/e2e/qa-lab/runtime/gateway-codex-refusal-product-proof.e2e.test.ts
GOMEMLIMIT=4GiB GOMAXPROCS=1 node scripts/run-oxlint.mjs --tsconfig extensions/tsconfig.json extensions/codex/src/app-server/run-attempt-finalize.ts
OPENCLAW_BUILD_PRIVATE_QA=1 OPENCLAW_BUNDLED_PLUGIN_BUILD_IDS=codex,openai,qa-lab,qa-channel NODE_OPTIONS=--max-old-space-size=6144 node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs scripts/build-all.mts qaRuntime
```

Results: 54 affected focused tests, four Gateway scenarios, lint and build pass. Formatting and contribution ratchets pass. Production +21 lines; tests/support +118; docs +13.

The independent runtime pass did not fault-inject every hidden lifecycle/configuration or direct-input/confirmation guard; those remain covered by source and focused regression evidence. First-time adoption or changed generic configuration of a loaded failed thread still requires native unloading. No real policy refusal was requested or overridden.

Thanks @Colton-Harris! Landed in [64c543a78b7fe2497bb40e5b73c47483e900ff06](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/64c543a78b7fe2497bb40e5b73c47483e900ff06), with your contributor credit retained.

**Proof:** Real Gateway and pinned native Codex HTTP401 recovery, independent ordinary/manual continuation and ownership rejection, plus harmless terminal/retry protocol controls. [Exact-head CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/33982203491), 54 affected focused tests, four Gateway scenarios and both reviews passed for [dda04893deb433098864bc65a6fdf5208c0f4f3e](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/dda04893deb433098864bc65a6fdf5208c0f4f3e).

| Before | After |
| --- | --- |
| A completed native failure could block the next message as another active runner. | The same configured conversation continues on its original native thread. |
| Misalignment lost its refusal classification. | One visible refusal stops recovery and model fallback; normal retryable errors still recover. |

The existing configuration, ownership and native confirmation guards remain. No public SDK error, schema or configuration option was added. Issue #138835 is closed; the original #138846 is superseded by this verified replacement.
